text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: spike in TLS handshake failures and 5xx from Cloudflare edge for api.redwood.ai (multi-POP). Alert triggered at 16:07 UTC. Paging oncall.
Theo V: Seeing a bunch of 525 and client TLS alerts. Spike started ~16:05 UTC. Traces show clients timing out before cert exchange.
Maya R: Direct origin probe to LB is healthy (200). This smells like an edge-side TLS termination regression.
Evan G: Quick triage: Are there any recent Cloudflare deploys? Also check if DNS changes were made.
Cloudflare Support: Hi, we're seeing anomalous TLS worker errors in a subset of POPs. Engineering investigating; ETA ~15m.
Theo V: Reproduced from one failing POP via curl:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:104.21.33.12 https://api.redwood.ai/health
# result: TLS handshake aborted, no cert presented
```
Maya R: We have an alternate plan available: split-horizon DNS (geo DNS) to route flights to a different CDN for specific regions. We also have an unproxy (gray-cloud) fallback. Which has lower blast radius?
Evan G: Split-horizon to alternate CDN (pre-provisioned) keeps WAF and edge protections. Unproxy is fastest but exposes origin. Given this looks like CF-side, prefer CNAME-to-alt-CDN for affected geos first.
dns-bot: Pre-provisioned alt: api-alt.cdn.redwood.net (Fastly). Geo-records available for us-east/eu-west/apac. TTL=30s.
Theo V: Let's do a geo CNAME for us-east and eu-west to api-alt.cdn.redwood.net and monitor. We'll avoid exposing origin.
Maya R: Applying Route53 geo changes now.
```
# performed by maya.r@redwood at 16:12:03 UTC
UPSERT api.redwood.ai (geo-us-east) CNAME -> api-alt.cdn.redwood.net
UPSERT api.redwood.ai (geo-eu-west) CNAME -> api-alt.cdn.redwood.net
```
Evan G: Observability: within 60s the cohorts on alt CDN show successful TLS and requests succeed. Global 5xx rate dropped ~60%. Latency for alt cohort +40-120ms.
Cloudflare Support: Update: we pushed emergency rollback for affected POPs; partial recovery seen. We'll update when all POPs are healthy.
Theo V: Product Ops, preparing a brief status update for customers: "We are experiencing degraded API connectivity due to a third-party CDN edge TLS issue. We have temporarily routed some regions to an alternate CDN to restore connectivity."
Product Ops: Draft ready, please approve. Also sending targeted emails to enterprise customers.
Security Oncall: Note: CNAME to alt CDN does not reveal origin IPs. Good. Still review WAF rules parity and rate limits on the alt CDN.
Evan G: CDN Ops confirms WAF rule set mirrored; additional strict rate-limits applied for the failover cohorts.
Maya R: Logging timeline: 16:07 alert -> 16:10 CF ticket -> 16:12 geo-CNAME applied -> 16:13 success for cohorts.
Cloudflare Support: Final: full rollback complete at 16:45 UTC. All POPs reporting healthy. We recommend re-routing traffic back gradually.
Theo V: Plan for revert: staged geo undo: eu-west -> us-east -> global with 5m observation windows. We'll revert eu-west first.
dns-bot: Reverting eu-west CNAME to proxied Cloudflare now (canary).
```
# performed by theo.v@redwood at 16:51:10 UTC
UPSERT api.redwood.ai (geo-eu-west) CNAME -> api-redwood.ai (proxied)
```
Evan G: Canary (eu-west) looks healthy after 6m. No TLS spikes. Reverting us-east now.
Maya R: Revert applied for us-east. Monitoring.
Product Ops: Updating status page: "Provider rollback successful; we are gradually returning traffic to primary CDN and monitoring closely."
Security Oncall: Confirm WAF parity checks complete. No anomalies in traffic patterns; no origin IP exposure.
Evan G: 30m after full revert metrics within baseline. No customer escalations open.
Theo V: Post-incident actions: 1) Postmortem lead = Theo; 2) Update runbook to include geo-CNAME path as first-line mitigation; 3) SDK retry guidance for TLS abort codes; 4) Request CF detailed RCA and POP-level telemetry.
Product Ops: Scheduling customer post-incident email and status page follow-up.
night-oncall: Taking over monitoring. Handoff notes: if TLS handshake errors >8% for 10m, revert to alt CDN and page Theo.
incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated. Severity: Sev2 (partial customer impact).
Theo V: Thanks all. Leaving thread for timeline and postmortem notes.
